title: Lesson 7: The CAGED System
intro: The open chords C, A, G, E and D are also five movable shapes. Played up the neck in that order, each one joins onto the next, so together they show every place a chord can be played and where its roots are.

items: Play C major in all five CAGED shapes.
Find any chord in five places from its root.
Lesson 5 (open and barre chords) and Lesson 3 (note names).

blocks.alt: Five chord diagrams of C major: the open C shape, the A shape at fret 3, the G shape at fret 5, the E shape barred at fret 8 and the D shape at fret 10, with the root C marked red in each.
blocks.caption: C major in the five CAGED shapes, moving up the neck.

items: Step 1. C shape: the open C chord, x32010. Roots: string 5 fret 3 and string 2 fret 1.
Step 2. A shape: barre at fret 3, x-3-5-5-5-3. The root under finger 1 on string 5 (fret 3) is the same C as in the C shape; the shapes overlap there.

Step 3. G shape, around fret 5: 8-7-5-5-5-8. It is the open G chord moved up; the roots are on string 6 fret 8, string 3 fret 5 and string 1 fret 8. It is a stretch: many players play just part of it (the top four strings: x-x-5-5-5-8).
Step 4. E shape: barre at fret 8, 8-10-10-9-8-8. Root under finger 1 on string 6 (fret 8), the same C as the G shape's bass note.
Step 5. D shape, around fret 10: x-x-10-12-13-12. Root on string 4 fret 10.
Step 6. After the D shape comes the C shape again at fret 12, an octave up. Step through the example and notice how each shape shares notes with the next.

examples.label: C, A, G, E, D shapes

blocks.text: Find any chord in five places

items: Step 1. Pick a chord, say G major. Its open shape is the G shape. The next shape up is the E shape, barred at fret 3 (3-5-5-4-3-3), then the D shape around fret 5 (x-x-5-7-8-7), then the C shape around fret 7 (x-10-9-7-8-7), then the A shape at fret 10 (x-10-12-12-12-10).
Step 2. For any chord: find its root on string 6 (E shape), string 5 (A or C shape) or string 4 (D shape), and build the shape on it.
Step 3. Each shape also sits inside a scale pattern (Lesson 6). Soloing near a shape keeps the chord's notes under your fingers.

examples.label: G, E, D, C, A shapes

items: 4 min: C major in all five shapes, up and back down.
4 min: G major in all five shapes.
3 min: pick a chord at random (D, A, F) and find it in at least three shapes.

blocks.title: Shapes for G
blocks.text: Which CAGED shape gives G major with its root on string 5 fret 10?
solution: A root on string 5 with a barre is the A shape: x-10-12-12-12-10.

blocks.text: Sources: Goodrick, M. (1987). The Advancing Guitarist. Hal Leonard; Wyatt, K. & Schroeder, C. (1998). Harmony and Theory: A Comprehensive Source for All Musicians. Hal Leonard; Tagliarino, B. (2006). Guitar Fretboard Workbook. Hal Leonard.
